subject: Order Form & IP boundaries — HelioWorks procurement
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Silva <ana.silva@helioworks.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-21 09:12 -0700
Subject: Order Form & IP boundaries — HelioWorks procurement

Hi Ana — great to meet on the call yesterday. Attached is the latest order form draft (OrderForm_HW_v2.pdf) and our proposed MSA redline (HelioWorks_MSA_redline_v3.docx).

Two quick asks so we can keep procurement moving:
- Please confirm whether HelioWorks needs an explicit assignment of output/title for the UI-generated content, or whether a perpetual, non-exclusive license is sufficient.
- HelioWorks mentioned their product team wants to exclude model retraining on generated content. Can you confirm required wording (opt-out clause vs. affirmative carveout)?

Laura and Ben are on copy for legal and pricing context. If HelioWorks prefers, we can run the redline through legal directly next week.

Thanks —
Sergio
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrderForm_HW_v2.pdf (pdf, 152KB); HelioWorks_MSA_redline_v3.docx (docx, 48KB)
From: Ana Silva <ana.silva@helioworks.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom.hargreaves@helioworks.com>, HelioWorks Legal <legal@helioworks.com>
Date: 2028-04-22 10:04 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form & IP boundaries — HelioWorks procurement

Hi Sergio — thanks for sending these over. Quick notes from procurement/legal: 

- Our product team is focused on ownership for in-product generated content (customer-facing UI components). They prefer assignment of title for those outputs to avoid any downstream commercialization ambiguity.
- For retraining: HelioWorks is not comfortable with an open feedback/training license. They want an explicit carveout that prevents Redwood from using customer outputs or feedback to further train models unless HelioWorks opts-in.

Our legal team will redline the MSA and return by end of week. In the meantime, can you provide a short statement explaining how Redwood technically isolates training data from customer-generated outputs (even if the contractual position is a carveout)? That will help our internal reviewers.

Best,
Ana Silva
Head of Procurement, HelioWorks

Quoted: "We want an assignment of output title for UI assets and an opt-in model retraining clause."
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-24 08:37 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Order Form & IP boundaries — HelioWorks procurement

Sergio / Ben — forwarding Ana's note. Ana's ask is stricter than our standard order form. Two points: 

1) Assignment vs. license: assignment of title for generated UI assets materially changes downstream rights; our standard compromise is a perpetual, non-exclusive, transferable license that includes attribution and a limited right to productize. Assignment is rare and will likely trigger pricing uplift and legal signoff.

2) Training/feedback carveout: we can offer an opt-in retrain clause (customer explicitly enables use for model updates) + a telemetry/data usage clause that allows safe operational telemetry for system health (no content used for model training). We should prepare a short technical note for Ana describing our data pipeline safeguards: prefix-KV exclusion, customer-specific namespaces, and private-model flagging.

I'll draft a brief technical statement and a counter-redline option that keeps title as a license but narrows productization. Recommend we loop Jordan if we need procurement/legal escalation.

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

Attachment: suggested_technical_statement_for_helioworks.txt (will draft)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Silva <ana.silva@helioworks.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-26 11:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form & IP boundaries — HelioWorks procurement

Ana — appreciate the clarity. We're aligned on trying to avoid wholesale assignment. For speed, attached is a targeted counterproposal: 
- Keep "ownership" as a perpetual, non-exclusive license for outputs generated via the service for HelioWorks' products, with explicit downstream productization carveouts narrow by purpose (UI assets used within HelioWorks products).
- Add explicit opt-in language for model retraining and a separate short clause that permits operational telemetry for debugging (no content ingestion for training).

Laura has prepared a short tech note describing our isolation controls (attached). If HelioWorks legal still prefers assignment, we can escalate to a commercial exceptions review — heads up that procurement will likely request a pricing delta for assignment.

Would HelioWorks accept a staged approach: sign order form with license + opt-in retraining, with a recorded evaluation period and an agreed amendment path if they still insist on assignment after evaluation?

Thanks,
Sergio

Attachments: Helio_Tech_Isolation_Statement.pdf (pdf, 9KB); Redwood_counter_redline_MSA.docx (docx, 12KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Silva <ana.silva@helioworks.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-28 16:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form & IP boundaries — HelioWorks procurement

Hi Ana / team — Jordan here from Sales Ops. Thanks for the clear asks. I wanted to confirm process and timeline: 

- If HelioWorks returns a redline that requests assignment, please flag which clauses require assignment and whether it's limited to specific asset classes (UI templates, embeddings, model outputs used as product content). That will help legal price and scope the change.
- If you can accept the staged approach Sergio proposed (license + opt-in retrain + 90-day evaluation), we can insert a commercial amendment template that documents the pricing uplift and an RACI for escalation.

Proposed next step: HelioWorks legal sends redline by EOD Friday (2028-04-30). If assignment remains requested, we will set a 30-minute escalation call between HelioWorks GC and our Head of Legal + Commercial lead.

Short, actionable items:
1) HelioWorks: return annotated MSA with specific assignment-language highlights.
2) Redwood: we'll prepare the commercial amendment template and pricing delta matrix.
3) Both: share available times for escalation call week of May 6.

I'll track in the deal record (HW-2028-0428) and coordinate the DocuSign flow once language is agreed.

Jordan Blake
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
